correctness.rationale: For a>0,D>0,4D>T² and input (0,u), scalar x(t)=-u G(t)+a H(t), G=e^{Tt/2} sin(omega t)/omega>0 on (0,pi/omega). u=aH/G=F_delta(theta) has F_delta(0+)=0, F_delta(pi-)=infinity and F_delta>0, so analytic increasing inverse gives first left flight time tau(u). Independent symbolic differentiation verifies N_delta'=(1+delta²)e^{-delta theta}sin theta, M_delta'=sin theta K_delta and K_delta'=(1+delta²)e^{-delta theta}[(2+delta²)sin theta-delta cos theta]; N_delta>0. If delta<=0, K>0 and M>0, so tau is strictly concave; if delta>0 the bracket in K' changes sign once and K(pi)>0, so M decreases then increases and crosses 0 exactly once, giving tau'' positive then negative. This is a global calculus proof, not numeric sampling; T=0 agrees with arctan formula.
residual_risks: Only a>0,D>0,4D>T²; no claim for other equilibrium position, overdamped node, or period composed across multiple flow zones.
Finite trace samples do not prove uniqueness; sign analysis does.
